correctness.summary: The right-angled-hexagon cosine law gives an exact half-angle formula for each seam. Multiplication yields the closed Basmajian seam-mass identity; a product-to-sum identity yields the symmetric cuff-length formula. Strict convexity of a translated cosh sum proves Schur-concavity, and the range and sharp one-half bound follow exactly.

limitations: Only compact hyperbolic pairs of pants with three positive geodesic boundary lengths are covered; cusps appear only as limits.
The quantity is the contribution of the three inter-cuff seams, not the full Basmajian orthospectrum sum.
No Schur monotonicity is claimed for individual seam lengths.
The complete text of Basmajian 1993 was not directly inspected, and the 2025 prime-orthogeodesic paper was not exhaustively compared line by line.
Originality is to the best of our knowledge; equivalent older right-angled-hexagon or orthospectral folklore may exist.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: Classical hexagon trigonometry and Basmajian's identity are excluded from the novelty claim. Targeted searches did not locate the fixed-total strict Schur-concavity, exact range, or sharp one-half seam-share theorem. Doan-Parlier-Tan concerns a different Luo-Tan pants measure. Equivalent older folklore remains a substantive risk because the derivation is elementary.

review_statement: Same-model review: passed. Independent audit: not yet performed.

value.summary: The result orders the three-seam Basmajian contribution under arbitrary cuff-length majorization, identifies its full fixed-total range, and gives a sharp global upper share of one half of total boundary length.
